paper.title: DESI 2024 VI: Cosmological Constraints from the Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations
truncated_sections: Appendix A Comparison of results from DESI and combined DESI+SDSS BAO data
Appendix B Comparison to Planck PR4 likelihoods

result.summary: 本文报告了DESI第一年观测（DR1）中星系、类星体和莱曼α森林示踪物的重子声学振荡（BAO）测量所得到的宇宙学结果，在0.1<z<4.2的七个红移区间内提供了横向共动距离和哈勃率的稳健测量 [abstract]。DESI BAO数据单独与平坦ΛCDM模型一致，得到物质密度Ωm=0.295±0.015 [abstract]。结合BBN先验和CMB声学角尺度，DESI要求H0=(68.52±0.62) km/s/Mpc [abstract]。在扩展暗能量模型中，DESI与CMB或Ia型超新星的组合偏好w0>-1和wa<0，与ΛCDM的差异在2.5σ至3.9σ之间 [abstract]。这些结果为偏离标准宇宙学模型提供了 tantalizing 的暗示，并凸显了DESI等Stage-IV巡天在确定暗能量本质方面的潜力 [S8.p7]。

research_question.text: 论文旨在利用DESI第一年观测的BAO测量，在七个红移区间内稳健测量横向共动距离和哈勃率，以检验暗能量动力学、空间曲率、哈勃常数和中微子质量等宇宙学参数 [abstract][S1.p5]。研究动机在于，尽管当前关键宇宙学参数与ΛCDM模型大体一致，但暗能量动力学尚未受到严格检验，且存在哈勃张力等 tensions，可能指示超出ΛCDM的新物理 [S1.p3]。DESI作为Stage IV巡天，设计用于通过测量星系、类星体和莱曼α森林的成团性来显著改善宇宙学约束 [S1.p7]。

evidence.quote: We present cosmological results from the measurement of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in galaxy, quasar and Lyman- α \alpha forest tracers from the first year of observations from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI)
However, dark energy dynamics has not been stringently tested.
Such tensions, if not due to unaccounted systematics, may indicate new physics beyond \Lambda CDM.
Using BAO we can test for dark energy dynamics and spatial curvature, and in combination with other probes constrain the Hubble constant, the sum of neutrino masses, and the number of light species.

The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) is carrying out a Stage IV survey that was designed to significantly improve cosmological constraints through measurements of the clustering of galaxies, quasars, and the Lyman- \alpha forest.

method.text: 论文采用BAO标准尺方法，通过测量星系、类星体和莱曼α森林示踪物的两点评分函数来提取BAO尺度，并利用密度场重构来锐化BAO信号 [S2.SS3.p4]。为减轻确认偏差，实施了盲分析，在系统误差调查和管线最终确定期间隐藏真实宇宙学结果 [S2.SS3.SSS1.p2]。宇宙学推断使用cobaya中的Metropolis-Hastings MCMC采样器，结合CAMB玻尔兹曼代码，并对外部数据集（BBN、CMB、SN Ia）进行联合分析 [S2.SS5.p1][S2.SS5.p3]。

evidence.quote: This effect may be partially reversed using density-field reconstruction to estimate these displacements based on the gravitational field inferred from the observed tracer distribution.

To mitigate against the possibility of such biases unknowingly entering into our analyses, we apply a system of blinding our data, to conceal the true cosmological results during the period where systematic errors were being investigated and analysis pipelines finalised.
We included in the cosmological inference code cobaya the PantheonPlus, Union3 and DESY5 SN Ia likelihoods, as well as our new DESI BAO likelihoods.
All Bayesian inference is performed using the Metropolis-Hastings MCMC sampler in cobaya.

experiments.text: 分析使用了DESI DR1中超过600万个独特红移的星系、类星体和莱曼α森林样本，覆盖0.1<z<4.2的七个红移区间 [S2.SS2.p2][S2.SS3.SSS2.p1]。外部数据集包括BBN先验、Planck和ACT的CMB数据（温度、极化及透镜），以及三个Ia型超新星数据集：Pantheon+、Union3和DES-SN5YR [S2.SS4.SSS1.p1][S2.SS4.SSS2.p3][S2.SS4.SSS3.p2]。宇宙学推断在平坦ΛCDM及其扩展模型（包括空间曲率、常数w、w0wa、中微子质量等）中进行，使用MCMC采样并满足收敛判据 [S2.SS5.p3][S2.SS5.p4]。

evidence.quote: Overall, this analysis of the DESI Data Release 1 relies on over $6$ million unique redshifts, more than twice the number of redshifts considered in the final SDSS cosmological analysis.

The results used in this paper are derived from the BAO measurements and fits described above applied to each of the five tracer samples across 7 distinct redshift bins covering a total redshift range from 0.1 to 4.2.
In a flat $\Lambda$ CDM background model, the BAO distance ladder results determine $\Omega_{\mathrm{m}}$ and $H_{0}r_{\mathrm{d}}$.

We use as our baseline the temperature (TT) and polarisation (EE) auto-spectra, plus their cross-spectra (TE), as incorporated in the simall, Commander (for multipoles $\ell<30$) and plik (for $\ell\geq 30$) likelihoods from the official PR3 release.
In this paper, we make use of three different SN Ia datasets.
Table 2 summarises the cosmological parameters that are sampled over in different runs, and the priors that are placed on them.
Chains are stopped when the Gelman-Rubin criterion ${\rm R}-1<0.01$ is satisfied

findings.text: DESI BAO数据单独与平坦ΛCDM模型一致，得到Ωm=0.295±0.015和rdh=(101.8±1.3) Mpc [S4.SS1.p1]。结合BBN先验和θ*，哈勃常数被限制为H0=(68.52±0.62) km/s/Mpc [S4.SS1.p4]。在wCDM模型中，DESI BAO单独给出w=-0.99^{+0.15}_{-0.13}，与ΛCDM一致 [S5.SS1.p3]。在w0waCDM模型中，DESI与CMB或SN Ia的组合偏好w0>-1和wa<0，与ΛCDM的差异在2.5σ至3.9σ之间，具体取决于SN Ia数据集 [S5.SS2.p5]。中微子质量上限在DESI BAO+CMB下为∑mν<0.072 eV (95% CL) [S7.SS1.p5]。

evidence.quote: The 68% credible-interval results for these parameters are $\left.\begin{aligned} \Omega_{\mathrm{m}}&=0.295\pm 0.015,\\ r_{\mathrm{d}}h&=(101.8\pm 1.3)\,\text{Mpc},\end{aligned}\ \right\}$
in combination with BBN information, further tightens the $H_{0}$ result to $H_{0}=(68.52\pm 0.62)\;\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}\qquad(\mbox{DESI BAO\,+\,BBN\,+\,$\theta_{\ast}$}),$
We find $\left.\begin{aligned} \Omega_{\mathrm{m}}&=0.293\pm 0.015,\\ w&=-0.99^{+0.15}_{-0.13},\end{aligned}\ \right\}$
These correspond to preferences for a $w_{0}w_{a}$ CDM model over $\Lambda$ CDM model at the $2.5\sigma$, $3.5\sigma$ and $3.9\sigma$ significance levels, respectively.
while adding the DESI BAO data sharply reduces this to $\left.\sum m_{\nu}<0.072{\,\rm eV}\quad\mbox{\text{\parbox{113.81102pt}{\begin{flushleft}(95\,\%,~DESI~BAO+CMB). \end{flushleft}}}}\right.$

limitations.text: 作者指出，中微子质量上限强烈依赖于∑mν的先验选择，且在扩展暗能量模型中显著放宽 [S7.SS1.p7][S7.SS1.p9]。w0waCDM模型中对演化暗能量的偏好可能被过度解读，因为部分偏好模型可映射到不违反零能量条件的精质模型 [S5.SS2.p9]。此外，DESI与SDSS在0.6<z<0.8红移区间的BAO测量存在约3σ的差异，其原因尚不清楚，可能是样本方差涨落 [S3.SS3.p4][S3.SS3.p5]。作者还提醒，当前结果中与ΛCDM的偏差可能受到未考虑的系统误差或数据集间不一致性的影响 [S8.p7]。

evidence.quote: We also caution that the upper bound obtained is strongly dependent on the choice of prior for $\sum m_{\nu}$.
However, we repeat the caveat that the limits are substantially relaxed in more extended dark energy models that affect the background geometry, such as those in Section 5.

However, we caution against over-interpretation of this result, since at least some of the $\left(w_{0},w_{a}\right)$ models preferred by our analysis could be mapped to quintessence models which reproduce the observable quantities $D_{M}/r_{d}$ and $D_{H}/r_{d}$ to high precision even though they do not violate the null energy condition at any redshift
the discrepancy between the DESI and SDSS results in the $0.6<z<0.8$ redshift range is at roughly the $\sim 3\sigma$ level.
The cause of this difference is not clear.
It remains important to thoroughly examine unaccounted-for sources of systematic uncertainties or inconsistencies between the different datasets that might be contributing to these results.
